name: Anthony Munday
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Anthony Munday (1560–1633) was a London writer who worked as an actor, playwright, pamphleteer, translator of romances and, later, as the city's pageant-poet. He wrote the two plays about Robin Hood as Earl of Huntington (acted 1598, printed 1601) with Henry Chettle.
The two songs here are taken from the play's death scenes as printed in A. H. Bullen's Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age (1889), where they are credited to Munday.

poems.title: Robin Hood Borne on His Bier
poems.author: Anthony Munday
poems.collection: Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age, ed. A. H. Bullen (London: Nimmo, 1889)
poems.note: From The Death of Robin Hood, by Anthony Munday and Henry Chettle (1601).
poems.text:
Weep, weep, ye woodmen! wail;
Your hands with sorrow wring!
Your master Robin Hood lies dead,
Therefore sigh as you sing.

Here lie his primer and his beads,
His bent bow and his arrows keen,
His good sword and his holy cross:
Now cast on flowers fresh and green.

And, as they fall, shed tears and say
Well, well-a-day! well, well-a-day!

Thus cast ye flowers fresh, and sing,
And on to Wakefield take your way.

poems.title: The Song of Robin Hood and His Huntsmen
poems.author: Anthony Munday
poems.collection: Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age, ed. A. H. Bullen (London: Nimmo, 1889)
poems.note: From The Death of Robin Hood, by Anthony Munday and Henry Chettle (1601).
poems.text:
Now wend we together, my merry men all,
Unto the forest side-a:
And there to strike a buck or a doe
Let our cunning all be tried-a.

Then go we merrily, merrily on,
To the greenwood to take our stand,
Where we will lie in wait for our game,
With our bent bows all in our hand.

What life is there like to Robin Hood?

It is so pleasant a thing-a:
In merry Sherwood he spends his days
As pleasantly as a king-a.

No man may compare with Robin Hood,
With Robin Hood, Scathlock and John:
Their like was never, and never will be,
If in case that they were gone.

They will not away from merry Sherwood
In any place else to dwell;
For there is neither city nor town
That likes them half so well.

Our lives are wholly given to hunt,
And haunt the merry green wood,
Where our best service is daily spent
For our master Robin Hood.
